title: Redis Outage Causes Cache Miss Storm in Product Service
description: Redis cluster experienced a network partition causing primary node failover. During the 45-second failover, product-service experienced a cache miss storm as all requests fell through to the database, overwhelming it.
initial_symptoms: Redis client logs show connection errors
Cache hit rate dropped from 95% to 5%

evidence_catalog.summary: Cache hit rate for product-service dropped from 95% to 5% at 16:00 UTC
evidence_catalog.query_reference: SELECT cache_hits / (cache_hits + cache_misses) FROM redis_metrics WHERE service='product-service'
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate Redis cache hit/miss metrics

evidence_catalog.summary: Redis logs show primary node failure and failover election starting at 16:00:15 UTC
evidence_catalog.query_reference: SELECT * FROM redis_logs WHERE message LIKE '%failover%' OR message LIKE '%election%'
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate Redis cluster failover logs

evidence_catalog.summary: Primary database CPU spiked from 40% to 100% within 30 seconds of Redis failover
evidence_catalog.query_reference: SELECT max(cpu_usage_percent) FROM db_metrics WHERE instance='postgresql-primary'
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate database CPU metrics

evidence_catalog.summary: Traces show Redis GET returning connection error, followed by DB query for same key
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate traces showing cache miss fallback to DB

evidence_catalog.summary: Cache TTL configured at 300s; no circuit breaker or fallback for Redis unavailability

causal_chain.from_description: Redis primary node network partition triggered failover
causal_chain.to_description: 45-second Redis unavailability caused cache miss storm

causal_chain.from_description: All product requests fell through to database simultaneously
causal_chain.to_description: Database overwhelmed by 20x normal query load
Product service latency increased 100x, timeouts cascaded

contributing_factors: Cache TTL too short for failover duration

must_not_claim: Product service code change caused the issue
Database schema change caused the issue

misleading_or_confounding_signals: Product service latency spike (symptom, not cause)
Database CPU spike (downstream effect of cache miss storm)

required_checks.description: Check Redis cluster status and failover timeline
Correlate cache hit rate drop with Redis failover
required_checks.expected_outcome: Hit rate drops exactly at failover start

required_checks.description: Verify database load correlates with cache misses
required_checks.expected_outcome: DB CPU spikes 30s after cache hit rate drops

remediation_guidance.suggestion: Add Redis circuit breaker with stale cache fallback; increase TTL; add connection retry with backoff
test_plan: Verify stale cache served during failover
remediation_guidance.rollback_plan: Configuration change only; revert config if issues
